title: Chorizo, Egg and Hash Brown Breakfast Burrito
summary: A toasted flour tortilla filled with homemade guajillo-ancho chorizo, soft-scrambled eggs, a crispy hash brown, thick avocado and Oaxaca cheese, with a creamy confit-garlic jalapeño sauce.
notes: Video: 'The Perfect Breakfast Burrito' on the Joshua Weissman Recipes channel (UCUAg71CJEvFdOnujmep1Svw). Written recipe for the same dish: https://www.joshuaweissman.com/recipes/the-perfect-breakfast-burrito (serves 6, prep 30 min, cook 1 hour). The video states the garlic oil, sauce, chorizo, eggs and butter, and 'about six' burritos. Where the video and the written recipe differ, the video wins: chorizo vinegar 1/4 cup (page: 2 Tbsp) and salt 1 Tbsp (page: 1 Tbsp + 1 tsp). From the written recipe: 6 hash browns, 3 avocados, 6 large flour tortillas, 2 cups Oaxaca cheese (the page also says 400 g, which does not match 2 cups shredded; we use the cup measure). Our estimate: 1 tsp kosher salt in the eggs. Not counted: the jalapeño sauce and the garlic oil it is made from (drizzled or on the side; the sauce takes 1-1 1/2 cups of the oil, about 2,000-3,000 kcal for the batch), the frying oil for the hash browns, and salt, lime and flaky salt 'to taste'. Chorizo chiles use USDA sun-dried hot chile; Oaxaca cheese uses USDA whole-milk mozzarella. Guajillo weight (4 chiles, about 24 g) is our estimate; ancho uses USDA dried ancho (17 g each); árbol uses USDA sun-dried hot chile (0.5 g each). Hash browns use USDA plain frozen hash browns, unprepared, so the oil they absorb in the fryer is not counted.

steps.text: Garlic oil: gently cook the garlic cloves in the oil over medium-low (low if it bubbles hard) until soft and lightly caramelized. Strain, keeping the oil and the garlic.
Char the jalapeños over an open flame, 2-4 minutes, covered bowl to steam, then rub off the skins and remove the stems (and seeds if you want it milder).

Blend the jalapeños, egg yolks, lime juice and zest, confit garlic, cilantro and salt, loosening with cold water. With the blender running, stream in about half to three-quarters of the garlic oil until creamy. Adjust salt and lime; refrigerate.

Chorizo: seed the guajillo, ancho and árbol chiles, simmer them in water 3-5 minutes until soft, then blend with the spices, salt, garlic and vinegar, adding a little of the chile water to make a thick purée.
Knead the cooled purée into the ground pork. Refrigerate a few hours or overnight if you can.
Press the chorizo into a hot 12-inch skillet with a little oil, sear 2-3 minutes, then break it up finely and cook 5-8 minutes more, until crisp and cooked through.
Deep-fry the frozen hash brown patties at 350°F for 2-4 minutes, until golden. Drain and salt.

Whisk the eggs. Melt the butter in a nonstick skillet over medium heat, add the eggs, season, and keep them moving, taking the pan on and off the heat, until small, just-set curds form. Transfer to a plate.
Quarter, peel and thickly slice the avocados; sprinkle with flaky salt and lime juice.

On a hot flour tortilla, layer chorizo, eggs, a split hash brown, two avocado slices and Oaxaca cheese. Fold in the sides, roll tightly, and toast seam side down in a skillet over medium heat 1-2 minutes per side. Serve with the jalapeño sauce.
